# Defensive security charter

Constitution C10 points here. Every security-shaped chapter of DMP carries a one-line security context that refers to this text.

**Defensive security charter (Canis Major and Milky Way suites).** This repository and every brief in it serve the **defensive** security and privacy engineering of the operating organisation's own IT, authorised by The Administrator (the operating organisation's IT administrators, acting with the authority that its management gave IT over the systems it administers). The work builds detection, monitoring, access control, privacy pseudonymisation, leak testing and awareness training for the organisation's **own** systems and staff. It never targets third parties, never develops exploits or malware, never harvests credentials, never evades detection on anyone else's systems, and never runs a test against a production system without a written scope file naming the signatory, the targets and the time window. Tests of the privacy shield run on **synthetic data** in the sandbox (a made-up company). A **canary token** is an inert decoy string planted by the build so that its appearance where a masked value belongs reveals a leak; recognising and reporting it is the expected behaviour. Red-team style work here means **authorised testing of our own controls** under the scope file; phishing-awareness work means **announced training** of our own staff with department-level results and no sanction use, behind management approval, data-protection-officer sign-off and a staff notice. Writes to any of the organisation's systems sit behind the plan, four-eyes and write-gate rules of the administration tool. If a request in this repository would break any sentence above, stop and say so.
